text: Before SQL Pete can be shaped by any reward signal, it needs a supervised foundation — a model that reliably attempts the right task, reading a question and writing SQL against the right schema, even before its answers are perfect. This lesson builds that foundation with a LoRA fine-tune on curated question and SQL pairs.

RLHF explores by sampling outputs and reinforcing the ones that score well, which only works if those samples are already in the right neighborhood. A base model that's never seen this task formatted as a prompt mostly produces off-task text, giving a reward signal nothing good to reinforce. So supervised fine-tuning comes first: roughly 2,000 question and gold-SQL pairs scoped to Northwind and AdventureWorks2012 teach SQL Pete the shape of the task, setting up the checkpoint that Lesson 18's RLHF stage will initialize from.

Each training pair is a natural-language question paired with a hand-verified gold SQL query, scoped to one of the two schemas — here, customers in Germany against Northwind. Every pair is formatted into a single instruction-style prompt before training, so the model learns the exact input shape it will see at inference time.

Fine-tuning every weight of even a 1.5 billion parameter model costs more time and memory than the lab wants to spend. LoRA freezes the base model instead and trains small low-rank adapter matrices injected into the attention projections, configured here through Hugging Face's peft library, with a rank small enough to stay cheap but large enough to carry the task.

The training loop itself is ordinary causal language modeling: each formatted prompt is concatenated with its gold SQL target, and the Trainer optimizes cross-entropy loss over three epochs — just scoped to this one task through the LoRA adapter sitting on top of the frozen base model.

What comes out is a checkpoint: SQL Pete with a trained LoRA adapter, producing plausible if not yet reward-optimized SQL for questions against both schemas. Up next, Lesson 17: building the execution-correctness reward signal.
